Alex: heads-up — we're seeing a cluster of SCIM 403s after yesterday's key rewrap job. customers report user membership missing in-app :frowning:
Maria: which idp? okta, azure, or both?
Alex: looks like both. first hit was an Okta tenant. logs show KMS decrypt errors on the provisioning worker.
Kevin: can you paste the error snippet?
Alex: sure — from provisioning-worker-3:
```
2026-03-22T02:11:05Z ERROR scim: provision_failed tenant=acme-corp uid=U12345 err="kms:Decrypt failed: invalid envelope header"
x-audit-id=evt-9f3a
```
Maria: that "invalid envelope header" smells like envelope rewrap mismatch. Did the rewrap roll forward aliases?
Priya: I ran the scheduled rewrap yesterday morning (rotation job). We rewrapped to alias/redwood-prod-2026-03 and removed the old alias immediately after. maybe too aggressive.
Kevin: if the provisioning worker still had cached ciphertexts created under the old alias, KMS Unwrap will fail after old alias removal. We should check the rewrap logs for the migration window.
infra-bot: rewrap-job-2026-03-21 completed; old-alias-scheduled-delete=true; total-keys=1; affected-buckets=2
Maria: do we have any queued provisioning retries? they might be trying to decrypt stale payloads.
Alex: yes — backlog spike on the scim queue, retries every 30s. first_message_ts=2743210987 -> last retry seen 2743210998. I've paused retries for tenants hitting repeated decrypt errors.
Priya: immediate mitigation: re-create temporary alias pointing to prior key material OR re-import the old envelope context if we still have it in S3. We kept old envelopes in blobstore for 7 days.
Kevin: good call. Before doing alias surgery, let's do a safe experiment on staging: rewrap a staging key and remove alias to replicate failure mode.
Alex: staging repro: created envelope with old-alias, removed alias, plugin fails on decrypt — exact match.
Maria: okay plan: (1) create short-lived alias old-alias-temp -> point to previous key version (2) unpause retries for 1 tenant, confirm decrypt success (3) run backfill for any failed membership updates (4) add telemetry to detect decrypt-failure-rate
Priya: I can create old-alias-temp but need approval from infra-owner. tagging @Kevin for sign-off.
Kevin: approved. Priya go ahead, but set TTL on alias to 1 hour and document in runbook.
Alex: after alias restore, provisioning worker logs show success:
```
2026-03-22T03:05:22Z INFO scim: provision_succeeded tenant=acme-corp uid=U12345 x-audit-id=evt-9f3a
```
Maria: great — but we need longer-term fixes: 1) change rewrap job to keep old alias for 48h and coordinate with retry windows; 2) mark envelopes with alias version in metadata so workers can detect stale; 3) improve audit logs so that x-audit-id surfaces in customer support view.
Priya: I'll open a PR for rewrap change and runbook edit. Alex — can you collect a sample set of affected tenants and share with support?
Alex: already pulled list: 12 tenants affected, 3 with high severity. I'll DM support with x-audit-ids and timestamps.
Kevin: also consider adding a proactive metric that fires when decrypt_failure_rate > 0.5% over 5m for scim workers.
Maria: agreed. Also add an incident tag to affected customers and notify account teams.
infra-bot: created incident INC-2026-03-22-kms-rewrap; owner=Priya; severity=high
Alex: follow-ups assigned: Priya — alias TTL & runbook + PR; Kevin — staging test and sign-off; Maria — telemetry + support notify; Alex — customer list + backfill script.
Priya: started the PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/compare/rewrap-retention
Kevin: I'll run the staging experiment and post results here.
Alex: thanks all. we should keep the alias temp in place until backfill completes.
Maria: one more ask: add a dashboard card for "scim.decrypt.failures" so paging on-call can see it immediately.
Kevin: doing that after my tests. ETA 2h.
Alex: closing the loop later today with a postmortem note. tagging @everyone for visibility :white_check_mark:
